gaps.sentence: He spent three years in ___ United States.
We had ___ lunch at a bistro near the cathedral.
gaps.explanation: Names of meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner) take no article when used generally.

gaps.sentence: She earns her living as ___ journalist.
gaps.explanation: Jobs after 'as' take a/an: as a journalist.

gaps.sentence: This is ___ second time you've been late this week.
___ unemployed are twice as likely to suffer from depression, the study found.
gaps.explanation: 'The + adjective' denotes the group as a whole: the unemployed.

gaps.sentence: Mount Everest is ___ highest mountain in the world.
They elected her ___ chairperson for a second term.
gaps.explanation: After 'elect/appoint', roles take no article: elected her chairperson.

gaps.sentence: They're building ___ new library near the town hall.
gaps.explanation: A new library — first mention; the town hall is the known one.
